authored_from: Articles (Serious)/technical/3B1B — Curated UI, §§1–5 (widget schema, β, compose(r), salience, knapsack); Cowan 2001 (K ≈ 4); Hick 1952 / Hyman 1953 (choice cost); measured against the Slice-13 Python implementation in sustena/core/curated_ui.py
note: ★★ The Rust build of what Slice 13 shipped in Python, so this row has a **reference implementation to measure against** rather than only a spec. The algorithm is at parity on purpose; the sharpenings are three, and each closes a gaming surface the reference left open.

★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★_1_there_is_NO_EventClass_in_this_core_: ★★ Checked first, because β's key depends on it. `EventClass` and `event_class` are **grep-0** in `sustena-core/src`; the Rust `Event` carries `name: String` and nothing that could serve as a class. ★ And the reference's `event_class` is **also just a string** — `WidgetSchema.binding_key` returns either that string or a `UNIT` sentinel, both used as plain `dict` keys. So there was no type to port, and inventing an `EventClass` taxonomy would have been this core deciding how the reference should have named its events. β keys on `Event.name` directly.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_2_the_one_sharpening_that_IS_worth_it: ★★ `BindingKey::{Unit, Event(String)}` makes `EventClass ∪ Unit` genuinely the ∪ the notation claims, rather than a magic string sharing a namespace with real event names. ★ Two effects, and the second is the useful one: the sentinel collision disappears (**theoretical** — nobody names an event `__unit__`, and it is worth saying that rather than dressing it up), and a widget with **no** binding becomes **unrepresentable** — which the reference has to reject at runtime with *'must declare either event_class or unit=true'*.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_3_UI_2's_typed_population_is_exactly_: `BindingTable::build` and `compose_view` take a **`WidgetSet`**, not a list of declarations — so every widget in β has already type-checked against `dim(S)` and `T`. **A widget with a made-up input cannot enter the knapsack**, because it never loaded. Doing UI-1 first would have meant a compose that ranks widgets whose inputs may not exist, and UI-2 would then have been a retrofit through it.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★_4_and_the_urgency_signal_is_ALREADY_HE: `region.rs`'s `Region::distance` returns `Distance { weighted, per_dimension, binding, relations_violated }` — the real weighted distance to `V`, with per-dimension excesses. The reference's urgency is an explicitly-declared **proxy** (`pct = spent/allocated`) and UI-7 says exactly why: *'deliberately reusing the Monitor's Slice-0 signal because CUSUM/EWMA don't exist'*. In this core they do.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_5_UI_7_reconcile_2026_08_17_the_blind: ★★★ Checked in code before touching anything, and it holds: **`spent/allocated` does not exist in this core's urgency path.** Every `allocated` hit in `sustena-core/src` is `budget.rs`'s operator writing real state paths, a `compose.rs`/`inverse.rs` test fixture, or the one docstring in `curated.rs` *describing* the reference's proxy. `urgency_of` calls `region.distance()` and nothing else. ★★ **There is no denominator, so there is no zero-denominator case to special-case wrongly** — the `allocated <= 0 -> 0.0` artifact is structurally impossible rather than fixed. UI-1 discharged it, and the honest move for UI-7 was to **say so and narrow**, not to re-derive a proxy that is gone. ★ The reference's *'unmapped captures pinned at 1.1'* constant is likewise **grep-0** here — a Python artifact of a queue this core does not have, recorded as checked.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★_6_the_GENUINE_residual_was_the_WEIGHT: ⚠ `pub const ALPHA_URGENCY: f64 = 0.75` — **exactly the defect UI-7's row names**: *'a policy living in a module constant'*. §IV is blunt: *'Nothing derives α = 0.75. It is a declared preference ... belongs in a declared constraint where it can be **argued with**, not a module constant.'* ★ And the precedent was already in this codebase: `Region::weights`'s own docstring reads *'A modelling choice, not a fact. Declared here so it can be argued with.'* The salience weights simply had not been given that treatment. `SaliencePolicy` is it.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★★_7_UI_13_reconcile_2026_08_17_the_THI: ★★★ Two of the three surfaces were already closed — **brightness** by MON-7 (field-relative, `VisualSpec` has no public constructor) and **score** by UI-1/UI-7 (urgency is `d(s,V)`, cost is derived, the weights are the household's). The third, **position**, had not been claimed by any row — and checking it found it **genuinely open**: `WidgetSet` is a `BTreeMap` keyed by id, `compose_view` additionally sorted candidates by `id`, and Rust's `sort_by` is **stable** — so wherever two widgets tied on score, the alphabetically-earlier **widget-authored id** took the higher slot. `aaa_spending` outranked `zzz_spending` at identical score. ★ Small, real, and exactly the Goodhart move the row is named for. So UI-13 is **not** a proof-only slice: it closes a lever.
★★_the_STEP_0_reconcile.★★★_8_CTL_8_reconcile_2026_08_17_a_CORE_: ★★ **Resolved in code: persistence is a core property, and the reason is that it needs NO stored state.** `compose_view` resolves fresh and keeps nothing, which looked like a tension with a *persistent* panel — but a persistent panel is not a remembered identity surviving a recomposition, it is an **unconditional inclusion by declared policy**, re-derived on every call. Adding the tier required zero storage, which is exactly what makes it composable here rather than host state. ★★★ **And the divergence expectation was wrong in the reference's favour and against it at once: `PANEL_POLICY` is grep-0 on BOTH sides.** It is not a constant dict in Python; it does not exist there. What the reference has is `PANELS` in `shell.jsx` — a **hardcoded seven-entry frontend nav list** for the Mycelium cockpit, with no `ALWAYS`/`WHEN_ACTIVE` distinction and no relation to Orchie's curated view. So the *panel list* exists as navigation; the *policy* exists only in the article. Recorded plainly rather than credited as declared intent in code.

divergence.statement: The algorithm is the reference's and is ported at parity: `score(w) = α·urgency + λ·relevance` with `α = 0.75` / `λ = 0.25`, a real 0/1 knapsack DP over integer cost and score×1000, `K = 4`, and `(selected, excluded)` both returned score-ordered. Three things are sharper, and each closes a gaming surface rather than adding a feature: **the ∪ is a sum type**, **the population is typed** (UI-2), and **cost is derived rather than declared**.
divergence.★★★_the_sharpening_that_matters_most_COS: ★★★ The reference's `knapsack_select` docstring says the cost model is *'Hick-Hyman's superlinear per-item cost — a widget with more inputs costs more attention chunks to parse, **see WidgetSchema.cost**'*. Following that pointer: `cost: int = 1`, read straight from the spec with `int(raw.get('cost', 1))`. **The formula is written down and never computed.** That is a gaming surface of exactly the `colour_rule` kind — a widget reading eight dimensions can declare `cost: 1` and get a bargain, while an honest widget declaring `3` is penalised for its honesty. Here `attention_cost` is **derived** from `inputs.len()` — which UI-2 already checked against `dim(S)` — and superlinear: `1 + n(n−1)/2`, the pairwise relating a reader has to do. ★★ It also closes the one hole share-of-`d(s,V)` would otherwise open: a widget **could** raise its urgency by declaring more dimensions, but the same declaration raises its cost superlinearly, so **the attention budget prices the strategy out** and the greedy move loses to two focused widgets. Asserted, not argued.
divergence.★★_the_counterweight_THE_ALGORITHM_IS_TH: ★★ This row ports rather than invents, and the thing being ported is right. The reference's knapsack is a **genuine 0/1 DP** — not the sort-and-take-N that would have been easy to ship and hard to notice — with the backtrack, the integer scaling and the excluded-with-scores return all already there, which is what makes *'N other things stayed quiet'* a true statement on the phone today. ★ `α = 0.75` dominant is its choice and is the right one. ★★ And the *no second notion of important* discipline is the reference's own and was honoured under pressure: Slice 0 derived the urgency signal, and Slice 13 **reused that formula verbatim** rather than inventing a selection-specific one. This core inherits a signal that was already single, and only substitutes a better measurement of the same thing. ★ Its urgency proxy is **declared as a proxy** in its own row, with the reason — which is why replacing it is an upgrade rather than a correction.

divergence.the_honest_limits: ★★ `render` STAYS OPAQUE, SO THIS RANKS RATHER THAN RENDERS — the output is a scored selection with its reasons, not a view fragment. The reference's `WIDGET_RENDERERS` are hand-written per render id and belong to a surface with a display; MON-7 drew the same line for the same reason. · ★★ URGENCY IS A **SHARE** OF `d(s,V)`, WHICH IS A MODELLING CHOICE AND IS STATED — a widget's urgency is the per-dimension excess it can show over the sustain's total, so it is relative to what else is wrong. A household with one breached dimension gives the widget reading it an urgency of 1.0; the same widget in a household with three breaches reads lower without changing. That is the intended reading (*the fraction of the trouble this card can show you*) and it is named so nobody infers an absolute. · ★ `relations_violated` CONTRIBUTES NO URGENCY — `region.rs` deliberately names failing relations rather than scoring them, because a boolean has no natural distance; so a sustain whose only breach is a relation reads zero urgency here. Inherited, correct, and worth stating: the widget layer does not invent the number the region layer refused to. · ★★ A ZERO-SCORE WIDGET IS NEVER SELECTED — the DP takes an item only when it strictly improves the total. That is right rather than a gap (`K ≈ 4` is scarce, and a card worth nothing is the noise a curated surface removes) and it is **at parity** with the reference; nothing is hidden, since it returns in `excluded` with its `0.0`. · ★ `device` IS CARRIED AND NOT USED — it rides in the request and comes back in the view, and ranking does not consult it. Naming a device-specific budget would be inventing policy; a host that wants one passes a different `budget`. · ★ RELEVANCE IS TOKEN OVERLAP, NOT MEANING — the same shape the reference uses, and it is the weaker term (`λ = 0.25`) precisely because the usual question is *what needs me right now* rather than a search. · AND NOTHING CALLS `compose_view` FROM AN ENGINE — a host assembles `r` and calls it, at a surface's cadence, the same seam MON-7 draws. · ★★ **UNDECLARED IS REPORTED, NOT PENALISED** — a widget reading only unbounded dimensions gets urgency `0` and an `Undeclared` basis; it is **not** given a floor, a boost, or a warning severity. Ranking it up would be this core deciding the household should care about something it declined to bound, which is the fabrication the whole row is against. The surface is told; the score is not touched. · ★ **THE BASIS IS PER-WIDGET, NOT PER-DIMENSION-OF-THE-SUM** — a widget reading one bounded and one unbounded dimension reads `Undeclared`, naming the unbounded one, even though its bounded half did contribute. That is the conservative direction (it flags that the reading is incomplete) and it is stated rather than left to be inferred. · ★ **THE SUM-TO-ONE RULE IS A CONSTRAINT ON THE ARGUMENT, NOT A DERIVATION** — it makes scores comparable; it does not make `0.75` correct. Nothing here derives the ratio, and the row's point stands: it is a preference, now held somewhere it can be disagreed with. · ★★ **A SURFACE MUST RENDER `rank`, NOT THE ARRAY INDEX** — the `Vec` necessarily has an order, and among peers that order is the household's declaration, which is *not* a ranking. A surface that draws position as prominence re-creates the very thing this closes, one layer up. The core reports the tie; it cannot force a renderer to honour it, and that boundary is named rather than assumed. · ★ **THE HOUSEHOLD CAN STILL ORDER ITS PEERS** — reordering the declarations reorders tied widgets. That is deliberate: the lever moved from the widget to the household, it did not disappear, and the household is the right owner. What it cannot do is change a `rank`. · ★★ **FLICKER-STABILITY IS NOT THIS ROW** — keeping a *dynamic* widget in its slot across recompositions to avoid churn is a genuinely different and harder concern: it needs memory of the last view, which is precisely what `compose_view` deliberately does not keep. CTL-8 is the always-shown tier; hysteresis on the competing tier is separate work, named rather than smuggled in. · ★ **THE CANONICAL PANEL LIST IS THE HOUSEHOLD'S, NOT THIS CORE'S** — §VIII names console, system health, IoT status and active sessions as the examples, and none is hardcoded here. A core that shipped its own list would be deciding what every household must always see, which is the same fabrication the whole salience family refuses. · ★ **A `WHEN_ACTIVE` PANEL IS INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM A WIDGET ONCE COMPOSED** — it merges into the same candidate pool and carries no marker in the view. That is deliberate (it *is* a widget) and it means a surface cannot style it differently, which is stated rather than left to be discovered. · ★ **GROUNDING IS PER-INPUT AND ANY-OF, NOT ALL-OF** — one resolving input grounds a widget reading five. That is the permissive direction on purpose: a card showing four of five things is still saying something, and requiring all would withdraw useful cards over one absent dimension. The conservative reading is available to a host that wants it and is not imposed here. · ★ **GROUNDING DOES NOT APPLY TO THE PERSISTENT TIER** — `ALWAYS` means always, so a persistent panel is shown even where nothing it reads resolves. Deliberate: the household declared it unconditional, and *nothing is here yet* is an answer a console is supposed to give.
divergence.★★_UI_7_the_blind_spot_is_the_PROXY'S_an: ★★★ The row's defect is precise and it belongs to the **proxy**: `pct = spent/allocated` is undefined at zero allocation, and the reference returns `0.0` there — so **an unfunded pocket that has been spent from scores as perfectly calm**, which is backwards. That is a manufactured zero. ★★ UI-1 replaced the proxy with `d(s,V)`, and **CASE A proves the fix rather than asserting it**: with `V` declaring the wall the pocket's spending drove state through (`balance >= 0`), the unfunded-pocket state reads a **non-zero** urgency and a `Bounded` basis. The metric the proxy was standing in for catches exactly what the proxy called calm. ★★★ **And CASE B is the finding worth carrying**: where `V` declares **no** wall on what a widget reads, `d(s,V)` is honestly `0` — but that is *the household declared nothing here*, not *nothing is wrong*. Rather than invent a wall to force urgency (which would be this core deciding what a household should care about), the basis is **reported**: `UrgencyBasis::{Bounded, Undeclared}`. Two widgets can read the same `0.0` and mean opposite things, and a surface can now say **silence** instead of showing calm. ★ The proxy manufactured a wrong zero; `d(s,V)` gives an honest zero, and this makes *which kind* legible.
divergence.★★_the_weights_are_now_DECLARED_POLICY_n: ★★ `SaliencePolicy::declared(alpha, lambda)` replaces the bare constants at the call site — the household passes it, and a **widget has nowhere to put one**, so the weights are argued with by the household and by nobody else. ★★ It **does** keep a `Default`, and that is the honest call rather than a lapse: `TrustPolicy` (IMM-10) has none because what a trust level may reach is a per-deployment decision with no safe answer, whereas here the article states a preference and it is a good one. The defect was never *there is a default* — it was *there is no way to hold a different one*. So the default survives, **named as a declaration rather than a derivation** in the constant's own docstring. ★★★ **Two things are not arguable, and they are refused**: `alpha > lambda`, because a policy letting a *search query* outrank *the household being in danger* would reintroduce at the weights exactly the gaming UI-1 closed at the inputs; and `alpha + lambda = 1`, so `score` in `[0,1]` keeps meaning the same thing across sustains and the DP's integer scaling stays interpretable. **You may argue the ratio; you may not argue urgency into second place.**
divergence.★★★_UI_13_the_THIRD_surface_was_ORDERING: ★★★ *Salience is never rendered as salience* has three surfaces a widget could stage its own prominence on. Brightness (MON-7) and score (UI-1/UI-7) were closed; **position** was open, and the mechanism was two innocuous things meeting: `WidgetSet` is a **`BTreeMap`** keyed by widget id, and Rust's `sort_by` is **stable** — so a score tie fell through to alphabetical order over a **widget-authored** name. ★★ Closed the way the other two were, by removing the lever rather than policing it. `rank_selection` orders on three keys a widget cannot set — **score** desc, **urgency** desc (so a search term cannot break a tie between two genuinely urgent cards), **cost** asc (derived from the declared inputs, and the right preference at equal value) — and past those the tie is **declared rather than broken**: peers share a `rank`, so **position carries no information the score did not already give**. That is the `Skew::Unknown` / `UrgencyBasis::Undeclared` discipline applied to ordering: do not fabricate a distinction you do not have. ★★ And the residual array order among peers is the **household's declaration order** — `WidgetSet` now keeps the order it was loaded in for exactly this reason — so **renaming a widget changes neither its rank nor its position**, while the household can still reorder its own peers. The lever moved from the widget to the household, which is the right owner.
divergence.★★★_all_THREE_salience_surfaces_now_cove: ★★★ Stated once, plainly, because the property is only worth as much as its least-covered surface. **(1) Brightness — MON-7**: field-relative across the field, and `VisualSpec` has no public constructor, so a widget cannot encode itself bright; it can only brighten by genuinely being further from `V`. **(2) Score — UI-1 and UI-7**: urgency is the household's `d(s,V)` (a widget's only lever is which dimensions it declares, and UI-2 checks those against `dim(S)`), cost is **derived** from those same inputs rather than author-declared, and the weights are the household's `SaliencePolicy`, which refuses to let urgency be argued into second place. **(3) Position — UI-13**: ordered on score/urgency/cost, ties declared rather than broken, and the residual order the household's declaration rather than the widget's name. ★ A widget can therefore raise its prominence in exactly one way, on all three surfaces: **by the household genuinely being further from its viable region on a dimension the widget declared it reads.**
divergence.★★★_CTL_8_two_tiers_and_the_persistent_o: ★★★ `view = persistent(ALWAYS) ∪ knapsack(dynamic, K≈4)`. A persistent panel is shown whatever else is happening, so it must **not** consume one of Cowan's four chunks — **a panel that could be displaced by a busy day is not persistent, it is merely high-scoring**. `View::spent` counts the dynamic tier alone, and the proof runs a budget of 1 fully occupied by a maximally-urgent widget with the panel present anyway. ★ `WHEN_ACTIVE` needs no machinery of its own: such a panel **is** a widget — eligible through β, selected through the knapsack — so the policy is two-valued with a real behavioural difference rather than a label with one live branch. ★★ **It carries no score and no rank.** Ranking a persistent panel would put it back into the competition it is exempt from, and a score would invite a surface to order it against widgets it never competed with. ★★★ **And it needs no stored state**, which is what makes this a core property rather than host state: re-derived every call, not remembered. ★★ **Exemption is the FOURTH salience surface**, and it is closed the same way as UI-13's three: `WidgetDecl` has **no policy field**, so a widget cannot skip the budget by claiming persistence — a `PanelDecl` is a wrapper only the household constructs. The widget's own declaration is byte-identical either way; what differs is whether the household wrapped it.
divergence.★★_I_p_is_DECLARED_not_computed: ★★ §VIII gives `I(p) = H(state | absent) − H(state | present)`, and computing `H(state | ·)` over a real sustain's state space is **intractable** in exactly the way MON-2's Kalman filter and MON-1's observability matrix are — both **declined imports** in this core rather than approximations. So persistence is a **declared policy** with `I(p)` as its **justification**: there is deliberately **no `information_value()` returning a number**, because there is no honest number to return. ★ `PanelDecl::always` **requires** a non-empty justification and refuses without one (`UnjustifiedPersistence`) — the argument is the only thing standing behind an exemption from the attention budget, so it must be written down to be argued with. Same treatment `Region::weights` already carries and `SaliencePolicy` gained in UI-7.
divergence.★★_UI_5_a_card_WITHDRAWS_rather_than_ren: ★★★ Found by the surface-block reconcile pass, and it was a **real residual** rather than something UI-1 had already covered. UI-1's event-first eligibility withdraws an *event-bound* widget whose class did not fire — but a **Unit-bound** widget is always eligible, so one with nothing to show still entered the ranking, scored `α·0 + λ·0.5 = 0.125`, and **was selected**, because the DP takes anything strictly above zero. That is exactly §III's *unexplained `0`*. ★★ Closed with a **grounding condition enforced before any ranking**: a widget is grounded when at least one declared input resolves to something real — present, non-null, and **not an empty container**, since an empty map or list is the *nothing to say* case exactly. Ungrounded widgets **withdraw**: not scored, not excluded-with-a-score, and **not counted in `candidates_considered`**. ★ **Derived, not declared** — from the same inputs UI-2 already checked against `dim(S)` — so a widget can no more declare itself grounded than declare itself cheap or persistent. ★ And the withdrawal is **reported** (`View::withdrawn`) rather than silent, because *never had anything to say* and *considered and outranked* are different facts: an exclusion carries a **score**, a withdrawal carries a **reason**.

beta_cases.name: ★_beta_keys_on_an_event_class_or_Unit_never_on_an_operator
beta_cases.why: ★ β is the formal **inverse** of the operator→widget `ui_schema`, and the type says so: `BindingKey` has exactly two shapes and neither is an operator name. Asserted by looking up a real operator (`budget.allocate`) and finding nothing — not because the lookup fails, but because β has no key that could hold it.
beta_cases.expect: Unit and the event class both resolve; an operator name resolves to nothing

beta_cases.name: ★★_an_event_bound_widget_is_NOT_a_candidate_when_its_class_did_not_fire
beta_cases.why: ★★ Event-first in **behaviour**, not only in shape. Absent from the recent log means the widget is never scored at all — not scored and ranked low. This is exactly what stops `compose` degrading into *scan everything and rank*, which is the failure mode the event-first framing exists to prevent, and it is checked by `candidates_considered` rather than by the selection.

beta_cases.name: it_becomes_a_candidate_the_moment_its_class_appears
beta_cases.why: The other half, and it carries **why**: the candidate's eligibility names the class that fired. A surface can say *this is here because a pocket was spent from* rather than *this is here*.

beta_cases.name: ★★★_a_widget_with_nothing_to_say_WITHDRAWS_rather_than_scoring_low
beta_cases.why: ★★★ The residual the reconcile pass found. A Unit-bound card reading an **empty** `pockets` map is not a candidate at all — not scored, not excluded with a score, and **not counted in `candidates_considered`**. Before this it scored `0.125` on relevance alone and was **selected**, which is §III's *unexplained zero* exactly. The grounding condition runs before any ranking, which is where the row says it belongs.
beta_cases.expect: considered = 1, withdrawn names the empty card, not in excluded

beta_cases.name: the_same_card_appears_the_moment_it_has_something_to_say
beta_cases.why: Withdrawal is about the state, not the card: put one pocket in the map and the same widget is a candidate again. A suppression that stuck would be a different and worse bug than the one it fixed.
beta_cases.expect: withdrawn when empty, selected when filled

beta_cases.name: ★★_withdrawal_is_a_DIFFERENT_ANSWER_from_exclusion
beta_cases.why: ★★ *Never had anything to say* and *considered and outranked* are different facts, and the view keeps them in different lists with different payloads: an excluded card carries a **score** it can quote, a withdrawn one carries a **reason**. Conflating them is what renders an unexplained `0`.
beta_cases.expect: one withdrawn with a reason, one excluded with a score

beta_cases.name: a_widget_declaring_no_inputs_is_grounded_by_default
beta_cases.why: ★ It makes no claim about state, so there is nothing for state to fail to support. Refusing it would invent a requirement §III does not make — the same restraint as not inventing a wall in UI-7's CASE B.

beta_cases.name: a_null_or_absent_input_does_not_ground_a_widget
beta_cases.why: Absent, `null`, and an empty array all read as nothing to say. Checked as three separate states rather than one, because *the key is missing* and *the key is there and empty* are different shapes that must reach the same honest answer.

beta_cases.name: ★_grounding_does_not_apply_to_the_persistent_tier
beta_cases.why: ★ `ALWAYS` means always. A console reading a dimension current state happens not to carry is still shown, because the household declared it unconditional and *nothing is here yet* is an answer. The interaction between UI-5 and CTL-8 is decided deliberately rather than falling out by accident.

urgency_cases.name: ★★_a_widget_reading_the_breached_dimension_outranks_one_reading_a_healthy_one
urgency_cases.why: ★★ Urgency is the real `d(s,V)`, restricted to what the widget reads. With `balance` 60 outside its band and `mood` inside, the money card carries urgency and the feelings card carries **exactly zero** — and the score ordering follows. This is the one signal the Monitor escalates on and MON-7 encodes, now with a third consumer, and no widget had a say in any of it.

urgency_cases.name: inside_the_viable_region_nothing_is_urgent
urgency_cases.why: `d(s,V) = 0` ⇒ every urgency is 0. Correct rather than degenerate: a household inside its own viable region has nothing urgent to show, and a surface that manufactured urgency there would be training people to ignore it.

urgency_cases.name: ★_a_widget_cannot_set_its_own_urgency
urgency_cases.why: ★ The only lever a widget has is **which dimensions it declares** — and those are checked against `dim(S)` at load by UI-2, so it cannot name one that does not exist. The distance itself is the household's, computed by `region.rs`. The same state read twice, breached and not, moves the urgency; nothing the widget does moves it.
urgency_cases.expect: urgency rises with the breach, not with anything the widget declares about itself

urgency_cases.name: cost_is_superlinear_in_the_declared_inputs
urgency_cases.why: `1 + n(n−1)/2` — 1, 2, 4, 7 — with the second difference asserted positive, so *superlinear* is checked rather than asserted. The justification is legible: reading `n` items is not `n` work, it is the pairwise relating between them.

urgency_cases.name: ★★★_grabbing_every_dimension_to_look_urgent_is_SELF_DEFEATING
urgency_cases.why: ★★★ The property that makes share-of-`d(s,V)` safe. A widget declaring all three dimensions captures the **whole** of the household's distance and scores maximally — and costs 4 chunks. Against a budget of 3 it is **excluded**, while two focused widgets costing 1 each are both selected. The greedy move buys the highest score at a price no budget can afford, so the attention budget prices out the gaming rather than a rule forbidding it.
urgency_cases.expect: the greedy widget excluded at cost 4; two focused widgets selected

urgency_cases.name: ★★★_the_proxy_blind_spot_is_gone_because_there_is_no_denominator
urgency_cases.why: ★★★ CASE A, and the row's own worry run as a test: a pocket with **zero allocation** that has been spent from, driving `balance` negative through a wall `V` declares. Under the proxy this is `spent/allocated` at a zero denominator, special-cased to `0.0` — *perfectly calm*, backwards. Under `d(s,V)` it reads **non-zero** with a `Bounded` basis. The metric the proxy stood in for catches exactly what the proxy called calm, and the artifact is structurally impossible here because **there is no denominator at all**.

urgency_cases.name: ★★★_an_undeclared_dimension_reads_zero_but_says_it_is_SILENCE_not_safety
urgency_cases.why: ★★★ CASE B, and the finding. Where `V` bounds nothing the widget reads, `d(s,V)` is honestly `0` — but that means *the household declared no wall here*, not *nothing is wrong*. **No wall is invented to force urgency**; instead the basis reports `Undeclared`, naming the dimension, and `describe()` says *silence rather than safety*. The proxy manufactured a wrong zero; this gives an honest one and makes which kind legible.
urgency_cases.expect: urgency = 0.0, basis = Undeclared { mood }, is_measured() = false

urgency_cases.name: ★★_an_honest_zero_inside_V_is_told_apart_from_an_unmeasured_one
urgency_cases.why: ★★ The distinction side by side: two widgets, the same `0.0`, opposite meanings. One is inside the viable region (calm); the other reads a dimension nothing bounds (unmeasured). Without the basis a surface would render both identically, which is precisely how a manufactured zero and an honest one become indistinguishable.

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_it_is_a_REAL_knapsack_and_not_a_sort_dressed_up
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ The case that tells the two apart: greedy-by-score takes the 0.90 item and stops at a total of 0.90; the DP takes the 0.60 + 0.55 pair for 1.15. A sort-and-take-N would fail this, and it is the difference between an attention budget that is spent well and one that merely looks ranked.
knapsack_cases.expect: the pair selected, the big one excluded

knapsack_cases.name: ★_the_selection_is_OPTIMAL_against_brute_force
knapsack_cases.why: ★ Optimality asserted rather than trusted: every feasible subset of five items is enumerated and the DP's total is checked equal to the best. *Every selected widget provably outscored what it displaced* is the whole justification for a person trusting the surface, so it is worth proving over the algorithm rather than over one example.

knapsack_cases.name: every_exclusion_comes_back_with_its_score
knapsack_cases.why: The *'N other things stayed quiet'* disclosure needs something true to say. An exclusion nobody can inspect is indistinguishable from a widget that was never considered — the same OPV-29 discipline that makes the Pareto frontier report what collapsing hid.
knapsack_cases.expect: the excluded candidate carries its score

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_a_zero_score_widget_is_not_shown_and_says_so_from_the_excluded_list
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ Found by testing rather than design, and kept. The DP takes an item only when it **strictly improves** the total, so a widget scoring exactly 0 never enters the selection. That is right — `K ≈ 4` is scarce and a card worth nothing is the noise a curated surface exists to remove — and it is **at parity** with the reference, whose `dp[c-w] + v > dp[c]` behaves identically. Nothing is hidden: it was considered, it is in `excluded` with its `0.0`, and `spent` is 0.
knapsack_cases.expect: considered = 1, selected empty, excluded score 0.0, spent 0

knapsack_cases.name: an_empty_field_selects_nothing_and_says_so
knapsack_cases.why: No candidates yields two empty lists rather than an error or a fabricated placeholder — the same honest-empty treatment the surface's own design language already uses.

knapsack_cases.name: the_default_policy_is_the_articles_declared_preference
knapsack_cases.why: The article's weights survive as the default a household inherits — named in the constant's docstring as **the article's declared preference, not a derived value**. The defect was never that a default existed; it was that there was no way to hold a different one.

knapsack_cases.name: ★_a_household_may_argue_the_ratio
knapsack_cases.why: ★ The point of the row: weighting urgency harder is now something a household can *do*, not something someone edits a module constant to change. A purely-urgent widget scores higher under a stricter policy than under the default, on identical state.
knapsack_cases.expect: the stricter policy raises the score

knapsack_cases.name: ★★★_urgency_cannot_be_argued_into_SECOND_PLACE
knapsack_cases.why: ★★★ The one thing that is not arguable, refused at construction. A policy where relevance meets or beats urgency would let a **search query outrank the household being in danger** — reintroducing at the weights exactly the gaming UI-1 closed at the inputs. Both the inverted case and the **tie** are refused, because *equal* is already a surface where a query can win.

knapsack_cases.name: the_weights_must_sum_to_one_so_a_score_means_the_same_thing_everywhere
knapsack_cases.why: Keeps the score on `[0,1]`, so it is comparable across sustains and the DP's integer scaling stays interpretable. A non-finite weight is refused too — the same absent-rather-than-defaulted discipline `Fraction::of` follows.

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_a_widget_cannot_set_the_weights
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ The policy is a parameter of the **household's** view: `WidgetDecl` has nowhere to put one and `compose_view` never reads one off the set. Asserted as the observable consequence — changing the policy changes the score and leaves the **urgency itself untouched**, so the un-gameable signal stays exactly as un-gameable as UI-1 made it.

knapsack_cases.name: ordering_follows_the_score_a_widget_cannot_set
knapsack_cases.why: The baseline: a widget named `zzz_urgent` reading a breached dimension outranks `aaa_calm` reading a healthy one. Alphabetically it comes last; by score it comes first. Ordering is derived from the one signal a widget cannot set.
knapsack_cases.expect: the urgent widget first, with the lower rank

knapsack_cases.name: ★★★_renaming_a_widget_changes_neither_its_rank_nor_its_POSITION
knapsack_cases.why: ★★★ THE PROPERTY, and the case that shows the lever was real. Two widgets tie on score, urgency and cost; rename one to sort first alphabetically. **Nothing moves** — not the rank, not the array position. Under the previous behaviour it would have jumped to the front, because a `BTreeMap` keyed by id plus a stable sort handed the residual tiebreak to the widget's own name. That is the Goodhart move, closed by removing the lever rather than policing it.
knapsack_cases.expect: identical ids in identical positions, identical ranks

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_a_tie_is_DECLARED_rather_than_broken
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ Past score, urgency and cost the two widgets are indistinguishable on everything the household can measure — so rather than fabricate a winner, they share a `rank`. **Position carries no information the score did not already give**, and where it would, the rank says so. The same discipline as `Skew::Unknown` and `UrgencyBasis::Undeclared`: do not invent a distinction you do not have.

knapsack_cases.name: ★_the_residual_order_is_the_HOUSEHOLD'S_declaration_order
knapsack_cases.why: ★ The other half of the rename case, and the reason the fix is honest rather than merely restrictive: swapping the two declarations **does** swap the tied peers' positions. The lever moved from the widget to the household — it did not disappear — and the household is the right owner. The `rank` is unmoved either way, so nothing about the *ranking* changed.
knapsack_cases.expect: declaration order decides among peers; ranks identical

knapsack_cases.name: cost_breaks_a_score_tie_and_cost_is_derived
knapsack_cases.why: At equal score and urgency the **cheaper** widget ranks first — the right preference (spend less attention for the same value) — and cost comes from `inputs.len()` (UI-1), so a widget cannot buy the slot by declaring itself cheap.
knapsack_cases.expect: the cost-1 widget ahead of the cost-4 one, and not a tie

knapsack_cases.name: ★_urgency_breaks_a_score_tie_BEFORE_a_query_can
knapsack_cases.why: ★ Two cards reach the same score by different routes — one urgent and irrelevant, one relevant and calm. Urgency wins the tiebreak, so **a search term cannot outrank the household's own distance-to-V** even at equal score. The same principle `SaliencePolicy`'s `α > λ` enforces on the score, applied to the ordering below it.

knapsack_cases.name: ranks_are_positions_not_a_dense_sequence
knapsack_cases.why: Two peers then a third gives ranks `0, 0, 2` rather than `0, 0, 1` — so a reader can see the third is genuinely behind **two** widgets, not behind one group. Competition ranking, because collapsing it would hide how many peers shared the top.

knapsack_cases.name: ★★★_a_persistent_panel_is_shown_against_a_FULL_URGENT_budget
knapsack_cases.why: ★★★ THE PROPERTY. A budget of 1, fully occupied by a maximally-urgent dynamic widget — and the persistent panel is present anyway, because it never competed. A panel that could be displaced by a busy day is not persistent, it is merely high-scoring, and this is the case that tells the two apart.

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_the_persistent_tier_does_not_consume_budget
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ Composed with and without the panel over identical state: `spent` is unchanged and the selected set is identical. The panel cost nothing and **displaced nobody** — which is the operational meaning of *outside the budget*, checked rather than asserted.

knapsack_cases.name: a_persistent_panel_is_shown_when_nothing_is_wrong
knapsack_cases.why: The point of `I(p)` being high for **all** states: *nothing is wrong* is itself the answer the panel gives. With no dynamic widget earning a slot the view is not empty — the console is still there, which is what a person opening the app on a calm day should see.

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_a_persistent_panel_carries_no_score_and_no_rank
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ Structural: `PanelInView` has neither field. Ranking it would put it back into the competition it is exempt from, and a score would invite a surface to order it against widgets it never competed with. What it does carry is the household's **justification**, so a surface can say *why* it is always there.
knapsack_cases.expect: no score, no rank, justification present

knapsack_cases.name: ★_a_when_active_panel_competes_like_any_widget
knapsack_cases.why: ★ The other half of the policy, and it needs no machinery: a `WHEN_ACTIVE` panel *is* a widget, so it joins the candidate pool, is counted in `candidates_considered`, and loses to a more urgent one under a tight budget. Two-valued with a real behavioural difference, rather than a label with one live branch.
knapsack_cases.expect: not persistent, but considered and competing

knapsack_cases.name: ★★★_a_widget_cannot_declare_itself_PERSISTENT
knapsack_cases.why: ★★★ The fourth salience surface — **exemption** — closed the same way as UI-13's three: by removing the lever. `WidgetDecl` has **no policy field**, so persistence is unspellable from the widget side; a `PanelDecl` is a wrapper only the household constructs. The same widget declaration lands in whichever tier the **household** put it in, and in neither by its own doing.
knapsack_cases.expect: identical declaration, opposite tiers, household's choice

knapsack_cases.name: ★★_a_persistent_panel_must_ARGUE_its_information_value
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ There is no computed `I(p)` standing behind the claim — `H(state | ·)` is intractable and this core declines to approximate it, as it declined Kalman (MON-2) and the observability matrix (MON-1). So the **justification is the only thing** standing behind an exemption from the attention budget, and an `ALWAYS` panel without one is refused. Written down means argued-with.

knapsack_cases.name: composing_twice_with_panels_gives_the_same_view
knapsack_cases.why: ★★ The no-stored-state resolution, asserted: the persistent tier is **re-derived** on every call rather than remembered, which is exactly why it fits a `compose` that deliberately keeps nothing — and why CTL-8 turned out to be a core property rather than host state.

read_only_cases.name: ★_compose_changes_nothing
read_only_cases.why: ★ Read-only **by signature** — shared references in, a `View` out, and no `Registry`, so there is nothing here that could run an operator. Asserted anyway across two calls, because a signature-only guarantee is worth exactly one refactor; the same doubled discipline EVT-15 applies to replay's effect suppression.
read_only_cases.expect: state and log byte-identical after two composes

read_only_cases.name: composing_twice_gives_the_same_view
read_only_cases.why: Resolved fresh on every call and **never stored**, so two calls on unchanged inputs must agree exactly — which also means candidate ordering is deterministic and the DP's tie-breaking is reproducible rather than incidental.

read_only_cases.name: relevance_is_neutral_with_no_query_and_real_with_one
read_only_cases.why: 0.5 with no query — the common case, since the usual question is *what needs me right now* rather than a search — and a real overlap fraction when there is one. The unrelated-query case doubles as the zero-score case above, which is how that behaviour was found.
